dropped.finding: A mid-IR optical bundle consisting of chalcogenide glass in the As-Se-Te system was used to connect an external beam port of a spectrometer to a grazing-angle probe over a distance of 1.5 m.
dropped.how_it_applies: This demonstrates that chalcogenide glass fibers can transmit mid-IR signals for probe coupling, though testing would be needed to see if transmission is viable over a 150 m distance.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited distance is 1.5 m in a laboratory or bench setup rather than a 150 m industrial installation, so attenuation over longer runs remains unverified.

citation.quote: The grazing angle accessory is connected to the external beam port of the Bruker Vector 22 spectrometer by a 1.5 m, 19-fiber chalcogenide glass optical bundle in the As-Se-Te system, which transmits throughout the mid-IR with the exception of a strong H-Se absorbance band at 2200 cm-1.
